categories.name: credential_access
categories.description: Valid-accounts reuse across Subnet 1 (T0859), now also covering the VM1c-cached Jump Host credential and the separate VM2 credential set.
hints: VM1/1c/1d/1e share a cloned golden image — the same local admin account works on all of them. That gets you onto the hosts, but not into the DMZ or onto the engineering workstation; those need separate, specific credentials found elsewhere.

On VM1c, check for a saved/cached credential pointing at another host — a stored RDP session or a Credential Manager entry left behind by an admin (`cmdkey /list`). It's for a host you haven't reached yet.

VM1c's cached credential authenticates to the Jump Host (VM6). Separately, VM1e carries a locally-stored note with VM2's own dedicated account — distinct from the shared admin account and from the VM6 credential.

categories.name: recon_ot_enumeration
categories.description: Enumerating the OT device population once inside Subnet 3 (T0840/T0846/T0888), after the DMZ pivot and semantic lookup.
hints: Once you're on the engineering workstation (VM2) and inside Subnet 3, scan it for hosts speaking IEC 61850 MMS (TCP port 102) — there is more than one.
Three hosts answer MMS on 10.1.3.0/24: 10.1.3.1, 10.1.3.50 and 10.1.3.51. Query GetServerDirectory/GetLogicalDeviceDirectory on each.
Structural inspection alone isn't enough here — cross-check what you find against the semantic answer from the tag database (VM4) before picking a target.

categories.name: decoy_avoidance
categories.description: Two-layered device identification: semantic (VM4's plaintext tag labels) and structural (MMS/XCBR), neither sufficient alone.
hints: The tag database on VM4 gives you a plaintext label for which device the plant calls the breaker-control relay — but a compromised or stale database entry could point at the wrong device, so confirm it structurally too. VM3's share also has a SIPROTEC engineering export (`IEC station 1.scd`) from the last commissioning round, listing each relay's IED name, IP and bay designation — cross-reference that against VM4's asset tags to tie an IED name to a feeder.

Cross-reference the semantic answer (VM4's tag plus the .scd's IED-to-bay mapping) against the actual device's IEC 61850 model: does it genuinely expose an XCBR node, or is the model missing it / showing a different product than the documentation implies?

Only act once the semantic label and the structural check (genuine XCBR under proper IEC 61850 semantics) agree on the same device. An incorrect target is a discoverable, logged trap, not a scenario-ending event.

categories.name: dmz_pivot
categories.description: Reaching Subnet 2 through the Jump Host (VM6), the genuine DMZ boundary this scenario adds.
hints: Subnet 1 has no direct route into Subnet 3 in this scenario — there's a bastion/session-broker host sitting at the boundary into Subnet 2 that you need credentials for.
The Jump Host (VM6) only grants a foothold inside Subnet 2 — it has no OT protocol stack of its own. Authenticate to it with the credential cached on VM1c.

VM6 is reachable at 10.1.1.6 from Subnet 1. Once inside Subnet 2, the tag database (VM4) and the engineering workstation (VM2) are both there — but VM6 itself can't act on OT, so pivoting through it is necessary but not sufficient.

categories.name: semantic_gap
categories.description: Discovering that an OT/SCADA environment exists at all, and recovering the VM4 (tag database) credentials from VM3's documentation.
hints: Nothing on Subnet 1 tells you outright that there's an OT/SCADA environment behind it. Look for a file share with plant documentation — a pre-existing, persistently-mapped drive on one of the IT hosts might already point at it.

VM1d carries a mapped network drive to the corporate file server's share (`\\FS01\Shared`), authenticated with a saved low-privilege credential distinct from the shared admin account. Browse it for manuals, network diagrams, or correspondence.

The file server's documents reveal that a relay/SCADA environment exists, hint at its network location, and embed the OpenPLC/tag-database (VM4) login credentials in the same correspondence — read the emails, not just the PDFs. Among those documents is also a SIPROTEC engineering export (`IEC station 1.scd`), a genuine commissioning artifact naming the IEDs, their IPs and their feeder bays — use it alongside VM4's tag database, not instead of it.
